methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: 3 or 4 data centers could be coming to a former coal mine site in Russell County
signals.signal_reading: Data center infrastructure arriving in Russell County's coal transition region signals capital concentration in extraction sites rather than capability distribution—physical infrastructure without local AI literacy creates economic dependency, not empowerment.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: Richmond Times-Dispatch op-ed explicitly identifies the core problem: Virginia debates data center real estate while small businesses lack AI adoption capability, signaling shallow engagement state-wide even as infrastructure concentrates in metros.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Workforce pressure on Richmond's young professionals suggests rapid platform-layer AI adoption creating productivity expectations without corresponding depth in AI development skills—distribution through tools, not understanding.

signals.title: Israeli AI maritime tech company joins Virginia Beach incubator - pilotonline.com
signals.signal_reading: Israeli maritime AI company joining Virginia Beach incubator reinforces Hampton Roads' defense-tech specialization cluster, deepening domain-specific excellence in military-adjacent sectors rather than broader regional AI capability.

signals.title: Virginia Tech researcher weighs in on threats, fears of AI development - WSLS
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech researcher engagement on AI development threats positions the New River Valley as a knowledge creation hub that could distribute understanding through educational networks—signals potential for peer-to-peer capability building beyond metro cores.
